subject: Conditional clauses and scoping for international data transfers (DPA Annex supplement)
messages:
From: Samuel Price <samuel.price@heliohealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T09:14:00Z
Subject: Clarification: conditional clauses in DPA annex for cross-border processing

Hi Sean / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HelioHealth’s privacy and procurement teams reviewed the standard DPA annex you shared. Before legal can proceed we have two scoping asks that affect the annex text:

1) We need a conditional transfer clause that limits EU->APAC routing to a subset of workloads (diagnostic inference only) and requires prior written notice for any expansion. Can you confirm how that would be captured in the annex and whether Redwood can enforce routing by workload tag?

2) For subprocessors: we require a named-subprocessor list plus an operational escrow-style fallback in case a subprocessor is removed and we need temporary access to logs for an audit. Is there an operational runbook or an attestation we can reference?

Attached is a short scoping PDF with our preferred clause language and two example flow diagrams. Can your team propose redlines or an implementation note?

Best,
Samuel
Privacy Lead, HelioHealth

Attachments: helio_scoping_requests_aug2027.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

Subject: Re: Clarification: conditional clauses in DPA annex for cross-border processing

Samuel / Asha —

Thanks for the clear scoping. Short answers up front:
- We can support workload-level routing policies (tags at the API/route level) and enforce EU-only routing for non-diagnostic workloads while permitting EU->APAC for diagnostic inference when explicitly enabled.
- We maintain a named-subprocessor registry; we can provide a monthly snapshot and a short operational escrow runbook for audit access (time-limited, logged exports).

I'll loop in our legal/ops folks with a draft annex that contains two options: (A) "conditional routing" language plus an automated enforcement note; (B) a more permissive routing framework with manual approval steps.

Deliverables we will attach in the next message: draft redline (docx), and an ops runbook PDF describing the temporary audit access flow.

Would you like the draft to use your suggested clause wording verbatim or to convert to Redwood standard phrasing?

Cheers,
Sean
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Clarification: conditional clauses in DPA annex for cross-border processing

Team — forwarding HelioHealth’s ask. Key points to address in the annex draft and ops note:

- Precise scoping: diagnostic inference = model name(s) + route IDs + data types (PHI pseudonymized/non-pseudonymized). Samuel asked about "workload tag" enforcement; ops needs clear identifiers we can check at runtime.
- Escrow/audit: legal wants to avoid wholesale escrow of data. Proposed compromise: time-limited export keys that require two-person approval and go to an encrypted, access-controlled bucket. Need steps and retention limits documented.
- Subprocessor listing cadence: they want named list + 30-day notice for additions, and a fallback for removals. We should propose a monthly named-subprocessor snapshot plus an SLA for notice.

Marissa / Karthik, can you draft: (1) the DPA annex redline focusing only on the conditional-routing clause and subprocessor paragraph; (2) a one-page ops runbook describing the audit export flow (approvers, encryption, retention).

Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Kimberly / team —

Drafted both items and attached: 1) dpa_annex_draft-conditional-routing.docx (redline and clean copy); 2) ops_runbook_audit_fallback.pdf (operational steps, scripts, roles). Changes worth flagging:

- Conditional routing clause includes a clear definition for "diagnostic inference workloads" by model list and route IDs and requires HelioHealth to provide a workload tag when enabling APAC routing.
- Subprocessor paragraph: we propose a named-subprocessor registry with a 30-day notice for additions, an exception process for emergency replacements, and a monthly export snapshot delivered to your security contact.
- Escrow fallback: instead of full escrow we propose an "emergency audit export" process: two Redwood approvers + HelioHealth security rep sign-off, data exported to a customer-controlled encrypted bucket for up to 14 days, full audit trail retained for 7 years.

Questions for legal: Are we comfortable with a 14-day retention window for the exported data? If not, propose alternatives.

Attaching drafts now. Happy to sync with Helio legal if you'd like a short call.

Marissa
Director, Product Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Kimberly / Sean —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear runbook. A few follow-ups from our legal/security team after internal review:

- The model-name scoping is good; we need one small change: expand the retention of the emergency export audit trail from 7 to 10 years for compliance with our records policy.
- For the 14-day export window: our Security team prefers 7 days unless we can get a documented extension process tied to a named approver. Could Redwood update the runbook to include an automated extension request workflow (Helio security triggers, Redwood approvers respond in 48 hours)?
- Subprocessor notice: 30 days is acceptable; add a requirement that any new subprocessor with access to pseudonymized PHI must complete a SOC2 Type II attestation within 90 days of onboarding.

If you can incorporate these three changes and send a redline, legal will review for final execution. We are happy to do a 30-minute call to close minor wording points — Asha and I are available Thu 10–11am CET.

Best,
Samuel
Privacy Lead, HelioHealth
